play_plan.meaning: The player's engine has stalled and the team is preparing the spare (T) car; the engineer tells the driver the car is done for now.
play_plan.when_it_should_play: Race only (SessionType 7, dword_7C56A4 == 7), player car only, when the engine has died (engine failure, not a crash or pit stop) and the car is stopped or coasting to a halt.
play_plan.trigger: ReasonCode (broker reason_code, veh+0x4068) == 1 (engine death, ENGINE_FAILURE.md:142, CONFIRMED) AND finish_state (veh+0x4064) == 0 AND speed (broker speed, veh+0x4440) < 2.0 m/s for 2.5 s. pit_status (veh+0x3450) == 0 (track). Read from F1CBrokerVehicleSnapshot fields reason_code, finish_state, speed, pit_status. Thresholds 2.0 m/s and 2.5 s are borrowed from the retire mod (DERIVED).
play_plan.subject: player (-1)
play_plan.technique: own_emitter: ERE queues PWS eid 112 after writing its cooldown (cooldown_unblock at 0x5C026C, FLT_MAX to e.g. 15.0). Use the queue and not sub_41B250, which would emit RETIRE lines.
play_plan.latch_cooldown: once per race (latch on first stall); 15 s event cooldown.
play_plan.must_not_play_when: Player already retired or DQ (finish_state != 0), car in pit lane or box (pit_status 1-4), car still moving above 2 m/s, a retire line (117-119) queued in the same second, and any time an MF line is pending on eid 112 (DD-07).
play_plan.conflicts: DD-07: mechanical_failures 1.0.7 queues eid 112 as its own token. ERE must check MF has no pending line on 112 before queuing; MF token move is a proposed follow-up. Native RETIRE04 (eid 119) also fires on ReasonCode 1 with the dwell, so the two lines can stack.
play_plan.calibration: speed threshold 2.0 m/s and dwell 2.5 s: DERIVED from retire_commentary_v5 (findings.jsonl:101), not measured for stalls.
play_plan.live_test: Owner runs an MF engine failure test on a race session (mech_test_panel.bat, feedback_mf_test_panel), stops the car, then checks the queue for eid 112 and the audio. Keep the test separate from the T-car idea.
play_plan.confidence: GUESS for the meaning and T-car behaviour (H3: T-car mechanic not in code, owner idea unproven). DERIVED for the trigger reads.

play_plan.meaning: The race is over for the player; the 'generic 2' retirement variant ('Your race is over'), same situation as PWS_RETIRE02.
play_plan.when_it_should_play: Only together with, or instead of, PWS_RETIRE02: race, player car only, after the retirement state of PWS_RETIRE02 (sub_41B250 path). Which of the two the game plays is UNKNOWN until the picker is found.
play_plan.trigger: Same as PWS_RETIRE02 (reason_code != 0 and not 1/7, finish_state == 0, speed < 2.0 m/s for 2.5 s after 10 m/s, race_phase 7). The score-115 picker that chooses sdt 119 over sdt 118 is NOT located, so no read decides it.
play_plan.subject: player (-1)
play_plan.technique: UNKNOWN. Do not add a carrier score: score 115 is also the RETIRE02 score, and the picker is not known. Once the picker is found, rotate score 115 only inside the retirement state; a new event-table row would be an owner decision.
play_plan.latch_cooldown: once per race (same latch as PWS_RETIRE02).
play_plan.must_not_play_when: In the same retirement as PWS_RETIRE02 when that line already played (no double retire line), DQ, normal finish, ReasonCode 1 engine death (RETIRE04 path).
play_plan.conflicts: PWS_RETIRE02 owned by pitstop_failures / player_retire_commentary (eid 117). RETIRE04 (sdt 121, eid 119) on ReasonCode 1.
play_plan.calibration: As PWS_RETIRE02: 10.0 s dwell (read live), 2.0 m/s / 2.5 s stop (DERIVED).
play_plan.live_test: First find out how the owner heard 'Your race is over' (the owner's 99-02 exe has cooldown 6.0 on eid 117, so a picker would be reachable there). Then retire the car in a race and see whether 119 plays alongside 117.
play_plan.confidence: GUESS. Picker existence is the open question (H8_orphans.md:17).
